To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have synthesized and characterized new cyclodextrin-hexaphyrin hybrids and demonstrated that the conformation of a hexaphyrrin can be switched by temperature or redox stimuli, leading to a change of the cavity coupling between two adjacent cyclodextrins.
we developed a novel type of sandwich hybrid with a hexaphyrinic device, which displays switchable redox and conformational states and thus behaves as an allosteric device.
we developed a new type of hybrid system that combines the properties of cyclodextrin and hexaphyrin in a single entity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of new molecular architectures based on cyclodextrins.
the design, synthesis, characterization and study of the properties of new hybrid materials based on cyclodextrins (CDs) and macrocyclic ligands (porphyrin, calixarene, etc).

the design, synthesis, and characterization of novel molecular architectures, with the goal of developing new materials and devices for applications in molecular recognition, catalysis, and electronics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work provides an unprecedented and original approach for the construction of a new class of hybrid materials, in which two different compartments are linked to a central device.
we have developed the first hexaphyrin-based sandwiched hybrid with two cyclodextrin cavities that can be reversibly locked and unlocked depending on the oxidation state of the hexaphylin.

the sandwiched hybrid is a dual-responsive double-latching device that can be used to regulate the association and disassociation of two cyclodexrin cavities, which are locked and unlocked depending on the redox and thermal states of the central device.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have designed a new type of hybrid molecule that is able to switch between two different states by using two different stimuli (redox and thermal) and thus can be used as a molecular switch or a molecular logic gate.
the hexaphyrins, which have been developed as a new type of porphyrinoids, have also been found as new type of porins.
we have developed an unprecedented dual-responsive device that is able to switch the communication between two compartments by a redox-triggered shape change.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed an original approach for the design and synthesis of molecular devices with two communicating compartments, which is a key feature for catalytic and regulatory functions.
the use of a central switchable device allows for a fine control of the association of communicating compartments.
we have designed a new family of heteroannulenes with switchable oxidation states, conformation, and aromaticity, and we have demonstrated their ability to act as dual-responsive latched devices.
